newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC okays new Alberta-Wyoming oilpipe rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC okays new Alberta-Wyoming oilpipe rates.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved proposed rates for a major new oil pipeline from Alberta, Canada, to Casper, Wyo., owned by affiliates of Alberta Energy Co Ltd and TransCanada Pipelines Ltd.
The Express Pipeline, which has yet to be built, is expected to ship 179,000 barrels per day of Canadian crude oil to the U.S. Rocky Mountain region.
This was the first time the FERC had approved an oil pipeline's rates ahead of construction.
Express offered shippers transportation contracts for 5-, 10- or 15-year terms, giving them lower rates the longer the term.
Companies which opted for the long-term rates will receive lower rates than companies that choose to use the line after it is built.
